test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 20% on the marked price of an item and thus gains 10%. What is the ratio of the cost price to the marked price of the item?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For problems relating Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) directly with profit and discount percentages, use the standard ratio formula:

Ratio of CP to MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

Substitute the given values (Discount = 20%, Profit = 10%):

CP : MP = (100 − 20) : (100 + 10)

CP : MP = 80 : 110 = 8 : 11

**∴ The correct answer is 8:11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount (D) = 20%

Profit (P) = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

Equating both equations for Selling Price (SP):

MP × (100 − D%) = CP × (100 + P%)

CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f544266250600692f4eaf584bf351fc2fd4fea2f87fcc43f8caeb5eb0a59767.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP / MP = (100 − 20) / (100 + 10)

⇒ CP / MP = 80 / 110

⇒ CP / MP = 8 / 11

**∴ The correct answer is 8:11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed or tagged on an article. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at cost price but uses a false or lesser weight, his profit percentage is given by: Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.
